item.title: Learn To Live:
item.content:encoded:
My review from the Art Exchange thread:

This is another very short story, this time about an interaction between Faeowynn and Dr. Everwood, Nico's other most-written character. So, they knew how to appeal to their audience! Fun fact, the person who wrote this asked me what my favorite tea was and how I would describe it… and that's how Chai entered this tale? I really don't know why my favorite tea had any bearing over Nico's gift, but, it did! So. There we go!

Still slightly confused why my choice of tea made it in, but you know what, I'm good with it. +1

item.title: Out of Frame:
item.content:encoded: I didn't get to write a review on this one before it went up, but this makes me intrigued enough that I might actually go back and read the rest of this series. After having read so much Conwell Content™️ to make my own gift for you, this absolutely reeks of Conwell. It has your style of dialogue, it has your style of action — because I didn't have context for how established any of these characters were but knew you were writing a continuation for a series, killing off that photographer felt like a pretty ballsy move. I do have to wonder… why anyone would care enough to destroy the photography department? I definitely have questions. But they're good questions. +1 and a wonderful gift.

item.title: SCP-5005:
item.content:encoded: i dont understand why something that exists in another reality is being classified as an SCP. TBH i couldnt be bothered to read through this entire massive wall of text, and the description alone gave me an internal sigh in the first sentence "located 3449 whalons to the Multiversal East of the Central Reality Compass and 87 whalons beyond where matter is ordinarily capable of permanently existing." what? was the point of this article to just string together as many words as possible, nevermind if anything you wrote makes any kind of sense at all? i got maybe 1/3 of the way down the page before i stopped. it just got worse with every sentence, like some guy was just sitting there with a thesaurus typing in whatever word he landed on at random. im sorry but if youre going to make up a bunch of fake concepts and objects, you need to put some effort into actually explaining them, otherwise its just literal nonsense.

item.title: SCP-5109:
item.content:encoded:
Thanks! After starting with a Euclid, which happened because the idea I came up with ended up being that, I intentionally wrote Safe, Keter, and Thaumiel next as I proceeded through all the recognized classes. I then went off the deep end with all the esoterics I could bundle together in my normal-length arms with relatively small hands, which is turning out to be nearly all of them. I think the classes work really well as creative prompts. If you were to come up with a Safe, what would it be? What would be so dangerous as to necessitate a Keter class? This isn't to say you should start with the class and then write the SCP — in most cases that's an abominable idea — but as an experiment, I've found it pretty inspirational. My highest-rated SCP exists because I forced myself to think: what's a Tiamat?

I had fun with the log format; SCP-5751 is a spiritual sequel in that regard. The idea of telling these mini-stories, and making them little puzzles for the reader to unravel, excited me. I've taken it up a notch in the companion tale series to this skip, starting with Character Development. Turns out the answer to the question I asked myself at the start of writing this article — "How many weird ideas can you think of based on an unforgettable password?" — is "a lot."

item.title: SCP-5109:
item.content:encoded:
I love Safe-Class SCPs. To me, low-security, low-risk articles require a hell of a lot of creativity to pull off and this one certainly delivered. Combine that with a surprisingly entertaining incident-log-ish section, an interesting anomaly, and a little bit of comedy, and voila! A fantastic and fascinating article!

+1
